A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SoliReward and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and six-page appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original annotation-agreement measurements, ID/OOD reward-model evaluations, ablations, and HunyuanVideo post-training results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds backbone/layer-selection evaluations and expanded post-training ablations in appendix Tables 11–13.

M1.justification: The binary annotation scheme, cross-prompt pairing, BT-WT objective, and HPQA attention and residual architecture remain unchanged in Section 3. Additional backbone and layer-selection experiments evaluate the existing method rather than introduce a revised procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 250k in-house videos, 50k OOD videos, and 20k prompts, covering physical plausibility, subject deformity, and semantic alignment. The ID/OOD evaluations and text-to-video post-training benchmarks are retained; additional backbone configurations do not expand data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The post-training comparison expands from v2 Table 10 to v3 Table 13, adding 'Yes' Token with BT and with BT-WT. HPQA variants using BT and BTT are incorporated from existing loss comparisons. The main reward-model comparator set in Table 2 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation configurations using Qwen2-VL 2B and Qwen2.5-VL 3B, layer-index sweeps including InternVL3 14B, and additional reward-head/loss combinations for post-training. These extend controls within the existing evaluation framework; retained metrics, split descriptions, training budgets, and implementation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 7.4 and Tables 11–12 test HPQA's layer-selection sensitivity and generality across VLM backbones. Expanded Table 13 separates reward-head and loss effects on overall Human Fidelity and its components. These substantially extend diagnostic evidence. The BT/BTT/BT-WT analysis itself already existed in v2 Section 9 and is relocated to Section 7.3.

E5.justification: The five-annotator agreement analysis and its reporting remain unchanged. New experimental tables continue reporting point estimates without model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; no new uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands results with backbone/layer-specific ID/OOD accuracies and margins, plus post-training component scores. For example, Table 11 reports 78.89 OOD accuracy for five-layer Qwen2-VL on Phy & Deform; Table 13 reports Human Fidelity of 0.8666 and 0.8861 for 'Yes' Token with BT and BT-WT. These are newly reported configurations. Main results and previously reported BT/BTT/BT-WT totals are unchanged.

T1.justification: The preference-order assumptions, BT and BT-WT losses, HPQA equations (1–6), and appendix win-tie suitability criterion retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about binary annotation, cross-prompt pairing, BT-WT, HPQA, and improved reward-model and post-training performance. The added experiments support existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Sections 7.4–7.5 add interpretations favoring four to five selected layers, HPQA applicability across VLM backbones, and a larger overall post-training contribution from BT-WT than HPQA. Section 5 removes the explicit sentence describing T2V-focused validation, although I2V remains future work and the appendix's win-tie applicability qualification is retained.

D1.justification: New Tables 11–12 specify exact HPQA layer-index sets and backbone sizes for the added evaluations. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning rates, training and inference settings, and code/benchmark access information are retained; the implementation tables move from Tables 11–12 to Tables 16–17.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Qwen2-VL, Video Generation Models Are Good Latent Reward Models, and Euphonium. It also replaces the Ford 2004 reference used for Krippendorff's alpha with Hayes and Krippendorff 2007. Research positioning and novelty claims otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes include author ordering, small grammatical corrections, a shortened limitations paragraph, and localized appendix restructuring. The existing loss comparison becomes Section 7.3, layer analysis becomes Section 7.4, and post-training becomes Section 7.5. Most explanatory prose and the main narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds two appendix tables, expands and restructures the post-training table, and relocates retained tables and Figure 7. These produce localized appendix layout changes. Main figures, plots, and qualitative comparison panels retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: Tables 11–13 provide useful evidence absent from v2 about backbone and layer choices and better separate the contributions of the reward head and training loss to post-training quality. This strengthens the method's validation and practical guidance. The principal experiments and conclusions remain unchanged, and the additions provide no uncertainty estimates, so the overall improvement is limited.
